liam: Quick writeup of a small prototype — Confidence-Gated RollForward (CGRF). Idea: use a tiny quantized proposer model (3B q4) to speculatively emit tokens, compute a confidence score (top2 margin normalized by entropy), and only run the heavyweight verifier (base 70B) when the score < threshold. want to capture notes + early bench.

anya: Sounds promising. gate metric = margin or entropy? how do you normalize across vocab sizes? :thinking_face:

liam: short: score = (logit_top1 - logit_top2) / (entropy + 1e-6). empirical scaling per model by median-entropy on calibration set. threshold tuned per rollout. goal: keep >90% acceptance to get throughput wins.

devon: Can the verifier reuse prefix KV to avoid full recompute when it needs to check a token? Ops-wise that matters a lot for latency.

liam: yes — we reuse prefix KV. verifier only runs forward for the candidate token(s) at that step (we keep full past keys). we tested both single-token verify and 2-token lookahead. single-token saves more compute but slightly higher false-negative rate.

zara: paste the benchmark command and a tiny result summary?

liam: ```
# bench script (dev pool)
python infra/bench_decode.py \
  --model=redwood/70b-base-q8 \
  --spec-proposer=local/3b-q4 \
  --gating=top2_margin_entropy \
  --threshold=0.9 \
  --batch=8 \
  --seq_len=512 \
  --profile=true
```

liam: quick numbers (avg over 3 runs, 10k tokens):
- baseline (70B q8, no speculative): p50=210ms/token, p95=420ms/token, cost=100 units per 1M tokens
- CGRF (3B proposer + 70B verify): p50=95ms/token, p95=250ms/token, cost=45 units per 1M tokens
- acceptance rate ~92% (single-token verify)
- quality: head-to-head win-rate vs baseline on HH-RLHF 1k sample = 48.5% (not statistically significant), delta in logprob on holdout = -0.02 avg

ops-bot: bench-ci: cg_rf_infra ✓ (k8s job 2026-03-20_14:22) :white_check_mark:

anya: interesting — p95 improvement is solid. any failure modes observed?

liam: a few. low-entropy, domain-shift prompts (long-context summarization, code completions with rare tokens) have lower acceptance and occasional quality regressions (fluency drops or hallucination where proposer overconfident). example below.

liam: SAMPLE: input (summarize long meeting notes)
- proposer (3B q4): "In summary, the meeting focused on timeline acceleration and marketing priorities. Action: team will deploy next week."
- verifier (70B): "In summary, the meeting highlighted risk around deployment timing, requested security review, and flagged three blockers: infra, compliance, and dependency on partner X. Action items: security review + partner sync."

liam: obvious loss of detail from proposer; gate missed it in ~3% of long-summary steps.

devon: can we hybridize: for long contexts increase threshold or force verifier every N tokens? also track token-level confidence drift (moving avg) to detect when to fall back.

liam: yup. we added "context-aware threshold" where threshold = base_threshold * (1 + 0.5 * (context_len/1024)) clamped. that reduced missed-detail cases but lowered acceptance to 88%. tradeoffs expected.

zara: next steps from ops: 1) run CGRF across quantization settings (3b q4 proposer vs q8 proposer); 2) run on ded-pool with batch sizes 1/4/8 for real p95; 3) collect per-route win-rate traces to feed Console. I'll allocate runs this afternoon.

anya: eval plan: holdout suite = HH-RLHF 1k, LongSumm 500, CodeGen 500. Metrics = head-to-head win-rate (human), pass@1 for code, coverage/recall for summarization, and delta logprob. Need also to log acceptance by token position and by prompt type.

liam: agreed. I'll add hooks to save a small delta sample set when verifier changes the token (store proposer output, verifier output, prompt, and gating score). format: JSONL for the eval harness.

devon: one more infra note: when proposer and verifier vocab/decoder tokenization differ slightly (we use same tokenizer but quant stack could change tokenization behavior) — we must ensure tokens align before reusing KV. assert in code: tokenization(proposer) == tokenization(verifier) for prefix -> failover to full verify otherwise.

liam: implemented that check. fallback to conservative mode if mismatch.

zara: logging: add a metric "spec.accept_rate" and "spec.quality_delta" per route, expose in Console, and raise alert if accept_rate < 80% or quality_delta < -0.05 win-rate.

liam: TL;DR: CGRF gives ~2x cost reduction and meaningful p50 improvements with modest p95 wins; quality impact is small overall but concentrated in low-entropy, long-context cases. threshold/context tuning and per-route configs make this practical for bursty workloads. Opening PR with code + eval harness now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/xxx (draft).

anya: great. please include a short README on threshold tuning and suggested defaults per route. also add tests that simulate tokenization mismatch.

ops-bot: scheduled: eng-ml/dedicated-run-6912345678 (ETA 3h).

zara: assigning follow-ups: @liam -> PR + sample dump, @devon -> KV align tests, @anya -> eval protocol + human AB plan. I'll create JIRA. :spiral_calendar:

liam: thanks all. I'll post results once the dedicated runs finish.
